blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back once the Stripe account is closed) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (The nightly settlement-worker can fail or not run without anyone noticing) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back that a redeploy alone cannot give. Paylane rejects authorizations or captures after the release (outage, misconfigured merchant account, a card network it declines). Every card payment fails, and the operator's only recovery is to redeploy the previous release. But from the next day the Stripe account is closed, so that release cannot take payments either: checkout stays down until Paylane is fixed. With weekly blue/green deploys, even a rollback on day one takes a full release. Keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (or a percentage rollout) for a set period, and close the Stripe account only once Paylane has run cleanly for that period. Write in the design the rollback procedure and the criterion for closing the account, and add a task for the switch.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back once the Stripe account is closed

findings.evidence:
It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Make the new worker visible when it fails. At 02:00 the Paylane API times out, the database is unreachable, or the CronJob is never scheduled (bad manifest, suspended job): no payment is reconciled, and nothing tells the operator. The only alert the plan defines (the finance channel, for an unmatched payment) fires only when the worker runs and succeeds, so a missing run looks the same as a clean night. Specify in the design a structured log at start and end of each run (date settled, payments fetched, matched, unmatched), a run-status metric or a last-success timestamp, and an alert when a run fails or no successful run happened in the last 24 hours. Also decide what a failed night does: re-run it safely (the matching should be idempotent) and catch up the missed days. Add a scenario to the spec and a task for this.
findings.title: The nightly settlement-worker can fail or not run without anyone noticing
